IMPORTANT PUBLIC HEALTH AND SAFETY MESSAGE REGARDING
PARTICIPATION AT CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS
AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

minutes_text:
MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  October 13, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:06 p.m. on October
13, 2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Mike Carroll*
  Mayor  Christina Shea

  * via teleconference

Mayor Shea announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications Local
Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of COVID-
19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all agenda items, which allowed members
of the public the ability to submit e-comments through the public comment portion of each
item and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City’s website.
She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was adhering to the Governor’s
Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and
equipment, as well as wearing face masks.
 City Council Agenda  October 13, 2020

  Mayor Shea also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items not
  on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m., which had been standard
  practice prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, and expressed her appreciation for everyone’s
  patience and understanding as the City continued to make adjustments to meeting protocols
  as needed.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Kuo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Malti Maheta, Founding Member of Indian Community of Irvine, provided the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Commend Janie Choi for Heroic Efforts

  Mayor Shea recognized Janie Choi, Irvine resident, for contacting
  emergency personnel about a fallen tree that resulted in a natural gas leak
  at the Woodbridge Village Shopping Center, and expressed her
  appreciation with a commendation for her heroic efforts.

  1.2  Employee Recognition - 25, 30, and 35 Years of Service

  Marianna Marysheva, Interim City Manager, recognized the following
  individuals for their years of service to the City of Irvine:

  •  Michael (Mike) Byrne, Senior Management Analyst (25 years)
  •  Pamela Duehr, Facilities Reservation Coordinator (25 years)
  •  Mike Hamel, Irvine Police Chief (25 years)
  •  Peter Anderson, Senior Transportation Analyst (30 years)
  •  Alex Mendoza, Police Officer (30 years)
  •  Nick Teague, Lead Street Maintenance Technician (35 years)

  1.3  Commend Public Safety Personnel for Outstanding Service to the
  Community

  Mayor Shea recognized the following Public Safety Personnel on behalf of
  Irvine resident, Ms. Nashashibi, for their professionalism and compassion
  in the handling of a recent investigation at a local storage facility:

  •  Nathan Ridlon, Detective
  •  Jodi Rahn, Community Services Officer
  •  Scott Foster, Community Services Officer
  •  John McDonald, Forensic Specialist II

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Agenda  October 13, 2020

  Mayor Shea also expressed her appreciation to Councilmembers Fox and
  Khan for bringing this item forward.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Local Recognition of Rights Award for City's Anti-Smoking Ordinance

  Mayor Shea introduced Dr. Dele Ogunseitan, Presidential Chair, Professor
  of Population Health & Disease Prevention at University of California, Irvine;
  and Dr. Bob Johnson, representing Non Toxic Neighborhoods, who
  presented the Local Recognition of Rights Award in recognition of the City’s
  Anti-Smoking Ordinance.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was none.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  Irvine is once again the Safest City of its size for violent crime, recording the lowest
  per capita violent crime rate for all cities in the U.S. with a population over 250,000,
  according to FBI data just released for calendar year 2019. It is the 15th consecutive
  year Irvine has recorded the lowest per capita violent crime rate for a city of its size.
  This success is attributed to several important factors, including: the tireless work of
  Irvine Police Department (IPD) personnel, residents who consistently work in
  partnership with IPD to prevent crime and keep our neighborhoods safe; and the
  support of civic leadership, both past and present, who have remained committed to
  Public Safety over the years.

  •  The City of Irvine has once again been voted as “Best City to Live In” in Orange
  County. This is the fifth consecutive year that Irvine has received this honor in The
  Orange County Register’s annual “Best of OC” selections. Register readers choose
  the winners in each category. Schools, public safety, recreation programs, parks and
  trails, exciting and diverse dining and shopping, and sports facilities all provide an
  unmatched quality of life.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Agenda  October 13, 2020

  •  Vista Verde School has been named a 2020 National Blue Ribbon School by the U.S.
  Department of Education, making it one of 367 schools from across the nation to earn
  what is widely considered the nation’s highest level of recognition for public and
  private schools. Thirty-six schools in California received this designation, with only five
  from Orange County. This is the second Blue Ribbon designation for Vista Verde,
  which was also recognized in 1996. Overall, this is Irvine Unified School District’s
  19th Blue Ribbon School dating back to the start of the federal program in 1983. Vista
  Verde was recognized for a culmination of different programs and initiatives focused
  on a positive school climate, positive student behavior, student academic
  performance, parent involvement, and a strong sense of family and community.

  •  The deadline to register to vote in the November 3 election is October 19. Eligible
  voters may register online at registertovote.ca.gov. After October 19, residents can
  still register and vote provisionally in the November 3 election. Provisional ballots are
  counted after elections officials have confirmed that the voter is registered to vote in
  the county and has not already cast a ballot in the election. In addition, registration
  status, ballot status, and more can be viewed at ocvote.com. The Orange County
  Registrar’s office has started mailing vote-by-mail ballots to all registered voters.
  Ballots can be mailed or placed in a Ballot Drop Box. There are seven Drop Boxes
  available in Irvine and even more throughout Orange County. In-person voting is also
  available at any Vote Center, 14 of which are located in Irvine, including one here at
  the Irvine Civic Center. Vote Centers will be open from Friday, October 30 through
  Tuesday, November 3. For more information about how you can safely cast your
  ballot, visit ocvote.com or call the City’s Election Hotline at 949-724-6159.

  •  Last month, Mayor Shea had the opportunity to join mayors across Orange County to
  create a video that drives home a very important message: “Mask up to open up OC.”
  All 34 Orange County mayors took part in the video that was filmed at iconic locations
  throughout the county. Orange County Mayors wanted to send a powerful message
  to residents, businesses, and visitors that we are in this together and we must work
  together to keep fighting coronavirus in our communities. With children back in school
  and more businesses reopening, wearing masks is more important than ever to
  ensure that progress is maintained, keeping cases low and preventing another
  shutdown.

  Councilmember Fox requested that an update on the impacts of COVID-19 on the business
  community by the Greater Irvine Chamber of Commerce, and City Council discussion on
  how the City could support local businesses, be added to the next agenda. Councilmember
  Kuo expressed his support.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Agenda  October 13, 2020

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  Councilmember Fox requested that Council Business Item No. 5.4 (Consideration of a
  request by Councilmember Khan and Councilmember Fox to reaffirm Irvine’s commitment
  to diversity, equity, and inclusion) by removed from the agenda to a date to be determined,
  to allow for a speaker to explain the intent of the proposed resolution. Councilmember Khan
  also clarified that the proposed resolution was not in relation to Proposition 16 on the
  November 3, 2020, ballot.

  3.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Councilmember Fox, and
  unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 3.1, 3.2, 3.6, and
  3.10. Consent Calendar Item Nos. 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.7, and 3.8 were removed for
  separate discussion. Consent Calendar Item No. 3.9 was previously removed
  from the agenda.

  3.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of a special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on September 8, 2020.
  2) Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on September 8, 2020.

  3.2  WARRANT AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 20-82 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING
  CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE
  FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID

  3.3  LICENSE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF IRVINE AND
  ORANGE COUNTY TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY - WIDENING OF

  Carl Petersen, Assistant City Clerk, noted that e-comments had been

  •  “Irvine Resident”

  This item was removed at the request of Councilmember Khan, who noted

  Marianna Marysheva, Interim City Manager, responded that the City

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Khan,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Kuo, and unanimously carried to:

  3.5  ACCEPTANCE OF CALIFORNIA OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY

  3.6  ACCEPTANCE OF 2020 ORANGE COUNTY OPERATIONAL AREA

  2) Authorized the Interim City Manager to execute the 2020 Orange

  3.7  NOTICE OF PENDING APPROVAL FOR TRACT MAPS IN ORCHARD
  HILLS

  Carl Petersen, Assistant City Clerk, noted that e-comments had been
  received from the following individuals in opposition to All American Asphalt
  continuing to operate its facility within a closed distance from neighboring
  communities:

  •  Peter Lin, Irvine resident
  •  Lesley Tan, Irvine resident
  •  Genny Guo, Irvine resident
  •  Kevin Lien, MD, Irvine resident
  •  Thomas Scott, Irvine resident
  •  Armond Ashgatugan, Irvine resident
  •  Emily Lynn, Irvine resident
  •  Channa Samynathan, Irvine resident
  •  Rose Wang, Irvine resident
  •  Meng Chen, Irvine resident
  •  Lina Chu, Irvine resident
  •  Dennis Lo, Irvine resident
  •  Chungliang Lee, Irvine resident

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether the City requires
  disclosure to potential homebuyers; suggested that maps be updated on
  the City’s website to include the All American Asphalt facility; and reiterated
  that the County of Orange approved the All American Asphalt permit in
  1994.

  City Attorney Melching responded that the City does not require disclosures
  at this time, but would work with Community Development as zoning maps
  were regulatory matters.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7
 City Council Agenda  October 13, 2020

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Kuo,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Fox and unanimously carried, to:

  Receive and file.

  3.8  APPROVAL OF PLANS, SPECIFICATIONS, AND CONTRACT
